title: Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line Module 1 Lesson 3: Slope Liquid Motion custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle slides down a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The particle is released from rest and travels a distance of $10\text{ m}$ down the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the acceleration of the particle and its speed at the bottom of the slope.

A particle is projected up a line of greatest slope of an inclined plane with an initial speed of $14\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The particle experiences a constant deceleration of $7\text{ m s}^{-2}$ while moving up the plane. Calculate the distance moved up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest and the time taken.

A metal ball of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest in air and reaches the surface of a viscous liquid with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. In the liquid, a constant upward resistive force of $3.6\text{ N}$ acts on the ball. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the deceleration of the ball in the liquid.

A sphere enters a tank of water with vertical downward velocity $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and decelerates uniformly in the water at $4\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the depth to which the sphere penetrates into the water before coming to instantaneous rest.

A particle is projected up a slope with initial speed $9\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along the line of greatest slope. It decelerates uniformly to rest in $3\text{ s}$. On a velocity-time graph with upwards along the slope defined as positive, determine the gradient representing acceleration and find the total distance travelled up the slope.

A small heavy stone enters oil with a downward speed of $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and decelerates uniformly at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until it hits the bottom of the oil tank, which is $4\text{ m}$ below the surface. Find the speed with which the stone strikes the bottom of the tank.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope of a plane inclined to the horizontal. While moving up the slope, the particle experiences a constant deceleration of $8\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the distance $d$ that $P$ moves up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest, and the time taken.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On the return journey down the plane, the particle accelerates uniformly from rest at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the speed of $P$ when it returns to its starting point, and the total time taken for the complete round trip.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at a height of $3.2\text{ m}$ above the surface of water in a deep tank. There is no instantaneous change of speed when the particle enters the water. In the water, the net upward resistive force produces a constant deceleration of $4\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the particle at the instant it reaches the water surface, and the time taken to fall through the air.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the depth to which the particle descends in the water before coming to instantaneous rest, and find the total time from release until it comes to rest in the water.

questions.prompt: A particle is projected from a point $P$ with initial speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope $PQR$ of an inclined plane. The distances $PQ$ and $QR$ are both equal to $2.4\text{ m}$. The particle takes $0.6\text{ s}$ to travel from $P$ to $Q$ and $1.0\text{ s}$ to travel from $Q$ to $R$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the deceleration of the particle is $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and find the initial speed $u$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the remaining distance the particle moves beyond $R$ before coming to instantaneous rest.

questions.prompt: A small metal cylinder of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $7.2\text{ m}$ above the oil surface in a large storage tank. The cylinder falls freely under gravity until entering the oil without sudden change in velocity. In the oil, a constant upward resistance force acts, bringing the cylinder to instantaneous rest after $1.5\text{ s}$ in the oil. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the velocity of the cylinder when it enters the oil, and the constant deceleration experienced by the cylinder while in the oil.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total depth reached by the cylinder in the oil, and state the coordinates $(t, v)$ of the three key points on the velocity-time graph from release until it comes to rest.

questions.prompt: An inclined plane $ABC$ of total length $30\text{ m}$ is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The upper section $AB$ of length $10\text{ m}$ is smooth. The lower section $BC$ of length $20\text{ m}$ is rough. A particle of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at $A$ and travels down the line of greatest slope $ABC$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the particle on the smooth section $AB$, its speed when it reaches $B$, and the time taken to travel from $A$ to $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the particle comes to rest exactly at point $C$, calculate the constant deceleration on the rough section $BC$, and find the total time taken to travel from $A$ to $C$.

questions.prompt: A small dense sphere of mass $0.25\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $4.05\text{ m}$ above the surface of liquid in a tank. The depth of the liquid in the tank is $3.2\text{ m}$. There is no instantaneous change in velocity as the sphere enters the liquid. In the liquid, a constant upward resistance force acts on the sphere, producing a downward deceleration of $5\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the sphere when it reaches the liquid surface, and the speed with which it strikes the horizontal floor of the tank.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The sphere rebounds vertically from the tank floor with an initial rebound speed of $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. While rising through the liquid, downward forces produce a constant deceleration of $15\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the height above the tank floor reached by the sphere on its rebound, and determine whether it reaches the surface of the liquid.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ is released from rest at the top $A$ of a smooth slope $AB$ of length $10\text{ m}$ inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. At the bottom $B$, the slope transitions smoothly without loss of speed to a second plane $BC$ inclined upwards at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = 0.6$. The plane $BC$ is rough, and the particle decelerates uniformly at $8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ while travelling up $BC$ until coming to instantaneous rest at $C$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the particle as it reaches $B$, and the time taken to travel from $A$ to $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the distance $BC$ travelled up the second plane before $P$ comes to instantaneous rest, the time taken to travel from $B$ to $C$, and the total time from initial release at $A$ until coming to rest at $C$.
